sources.role: config path, EEPROM default, snapshot storage

paths.path: ~/.local/share/xemu/xemu/xemu.toml (SDL_GetPrefPath("xemu","xemu")); portable mode uses xemu.toml next to the executable; -config_path <file> selects a private config and is auto-saved back at exit

Per-game saves live on the E partition of the virtual hard-disk image (sys.files.hdd_path, qcow2; the pre-built xbox_hdd.qcow2 is offered) plus eeprom.bin for console identity in the same base dir — nothing is written as individual per-game files, so syncing means copying whole qemu disk images (and possibly eeprom.bin, since saves may be tied to the HDD key/EEPROM)
paths.naming: No per-game save files: saves are FATX content inside the qcow2 HDD image; identity/config sidecars are eeprom.bin (auto-generated when absent) and xemu.toml in the SDL pref-path base dir
evidence: docs:faq "Just like on a real Xbox, they are stored on the E partition of the virtual hard drive"
docs:faq EEPROM auto-created and saves-tied-to-console answers

paths.path: QEMU VM snapshots stored inside the HDD disk image itself (Machine -> Snapshots UI, bindable F5-F8 shortcuts, monitor savevm/loadvm); they are not standalone files and capture discs/controllers/HDD state
paths.naming: Named QEMU snapshots embedded in the hdd qcow2 image (savevm names); the docs note the data "is not easily extractable" and reverting can hide newer in-game saves
evidence: docs:faq "Snapshot data is stored on the hard drive image, and is not easily extractable"
docs:snapshots "Snapshots are saved to the hard disk image that you started xemu with"

paths.path: User-dumped pair set via sys.files.bootrom_path (MCPX boot ROM, conventionally mcpx_1.0.bin, MD5 d49c52a4102f6df7bcf8d0617ac475ed) and sys.files.flashrom_path (BIOS flash from a 1.0 Xbox; debug or modded retail such as COMPLEX 4627 is required since unmodified retail BIOS cannot boot games); redistributable prebuilt xbox_hdd.qcow2 ships only a clean dashboard
evidence: docs:faq "Your MCPX and BIOS dump should be from a 1.0 Xbox"
contract:docs/XEMU_NATIVE_CONTROLLER_CONTRACT.md (user-declared MCPX boot ROM and flash image)

linux.notes: No xemu flatpak exists: a Flathub search for xemu returns no app (official channel is the AppImage). Lunchbox launches xemu with -config_path plus a private SDL pref path.
